A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Existing material can be matched across relocation and renumbering, including the additional legal-domain material in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original poisoning-attack results, embedding analyses, defense experiments, and ablations in Tables 1–4, Figures 3–9, and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds legal Q&A attack results in Table 2 and a synthetic medical-query experiment in Remark 2.

M1.justification: The query–payload concatenation attack and clean-anchor, shrinkage-Mahalanobis defense remain unchanged, including the detection threshold. Applying the attack to legal data does not introduce a new proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 extends actual evaluation beyond medicine to Australian Open Legal QA, with two synthetic legal payload categories alongside existing payload types. It also tests generated doctor-style medical queries derived from MedMCQA. The legal evaluation substantially broadens the represented application domains.

E2.justification: Existing norm/distance comparisons and defense testing against PoisonedRAG are retained. The added legal experiment uses existing retrievers, Contriever and SPECTER, without introducing a new competing attack or defense.

E3.justification: Remark 2 introduces a 100-query GPT-4-generated evaluation using Contriever on PubMed; the legal experiment evaluates top-2 retrieval with Contriever and SPECTER. Previously reported medical sample counts, retrieval inputs, top-K settings, and defense threshold remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new synthetic-query experiment examines whether attackers can construct plausible medical target queries that support successful retrieval attacks. Existing paraphrasing robustness, top-1 retrieval, and shrinkage-sensitivity analyses are retained; the paraphrasing table is relocated rather than newly added.

E5.justification: Both versions retain averaging over three target-document variants, the same dispersion bounds, and existing uncertainty displays. v2 introduces no new seed information, repeated-run procedure, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds legal attack success rates ranging from 0.78 to 0.92 in Table 2 and approximately 0.92 for the 100 synthetic medical queries in Remark 2. Matched original table values and plotted results remain unchanged. These are additional results under new conditions, not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The formal threat assumptions, orthogonal-augmentation reasoning, covariance-shrinkage definition, and defense-distance formula are retained. The new remarks discuss feasibility of existing assumptions without adding or revising a theorem, proof, or mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: Section 1.1 extends the vulnerability contribution from medical Q&A to medical and legal Q&A. The abstract also drops the assurance that the defense will ensure safe RAG use. The central attack, geometric explanation, and detection claims otherwise remain intact.

C2.justification: New remarks argue for threat-model feasibility using public medical databases and predictable medical query patterns. v2 removes the explicit limitations discussion, including the defense's restriction to targeted queries, although Section 5 retains its anchor-set assumption. It adds dynamic pruning as a future research direction.

D1.justification: v2 supplies query and legal-payload generation descriptions and an ALQA question–support–answer example in Appendix D. These additions provide limited implementation context, without exact generation prompts or legal dataset split sizes. Existing hardware, FAISS, and medical retrieval details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds a related-work paragraph connecting the study to three backdoor-attack and defense papers, plus citations concerning alignment, nephrology, legal data, and dynamic pruning. It removes Huang et al.'s covariance-estimation reference. The principal positioning against PoisonedRAG remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The revision makes localized prose edits, adds numbered remarks and Appendix D, updates author and affiliation information, and renames Section 3 and the impact section. Most exposition and the main section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds the legal-results table and legal-example table, moves v1 Table 2 to Appendix B as Table 7, and reformats several existing tables. Figures are redistributed and some resized, while their underlying visual content is retained.

improvement.justification: The legal attack experiment partially addresses v1's explicit medical-only evidence limitation, while the synthetic-query experiment adds a useful check of practical target selection. These provide modest empirical benefits while preserving the original analyses. Sparse documentation of the new experiments and removal of the explicit defense-limitations discussion temper the improvement; the targeted-query anchor assumption remains stated in Section 5.
